title: Core Roles
description: Covers the full scope of CHW practice: cultural mediation and humility (CLAS standards), health education, care coordination, client coaching, advocacy, capacity building, screenings, referrals, community assessments, outreach, and program evaluation. Grounded in the national C3 framework.
notes: Adapted from Calbright College CHW program outline (course 02 / CHW 502), renumbered per CCC convention.
lesson_length: Lab-guide lessons, roughly 1500-2000 words each, supporting instructor-led sessions and independent study
learning_objectives: Describe the C3 framework roles that define the scope of CHW practice
Explain cultural mediation and humility, including the CLAS standards
Describe how education, coordination, coaching, advocacy, outreach, and evaluation fit together in practice
prerequisites: CHW101: Introduction to Community Health Work

lessons.title: Cultural Mediation and Humility
objectives: Explain cultural mediation and humility, including the CLAS standards
Use language access resources appropriately in mediation situations

lessons.title: Health Education and Client Coaching
objectives: Describe the C3 framework roles that define the scope of CHW practice
Deliver culturally and literacy-appropriate health education and support client-owned goals

lessons.title: Care Coordination, Screenings, and Referrals
objectives: Match client needs to resources and carry referrals through to confirmed connection
Describe the CHW role in screenings and multi-provider care coordination

lessons.title: Advocacy and Capacity Building
objectives: Advocate for clients facing barriers and coach them toward self-advocacy
Build on client and community strengths to increase independence

lessons.title: Outreach, Assessment, and Program Evaluation
objectives: Describe how education, coordination, coaching, advocacy, outreach, and evaluation fit together in practice
Explain the CHW role in community assessment and program evaluation

sequencing_rationale: Course 2 of 6: the C3 role set. Cultural mediation first because it conditions every other role, then the service roles in client-facing order (education/coaching, coordination/referrals), then advocacy/capacity building, closing with the community-facing roles (outreach, assessment, evaluation). Scope assumption: this course covers roles at orientation depth — what each role is and when it applies; CHW103 drills the skills. CLAS standards taught inside cultural mediation.
